Rashi on Ketubot 17a:10:1.hebrew: אפילו למ"ד - פלוגתא בפרק קמא דקדושין:
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:10:1.english: Even [according] to the one who says - [This is] a dispute in the first chapter of Kiddushin.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:10:2.hebrew: שום תשים עליך מלך - ישראל הוזהרו שישימו עליהם שימות הרבה, כלומר שתהא אימתו עליהם. הלכך, אין כבודו מחול, שלפיכך ריבה הכתוב שימות הרבה:
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:10:2.english: You shall surely place a king over you - Israel were enjoined to place upon themselves many placings [of his authority], meaning that his awe should be upon them. Therefore, his honor is not relinquished, for that is why Scripture multiplied [the expressions of] placing.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:10:3.hebrew: פרשת דרכים הוה - ולא ניכר שעבר מלפניה, אלא כאילו הוא צריך לפנות לאותו הדרך:
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:10:3.english: It was a crossroads - And it was not noticeable that he stepped aside before her, rather [it appeared] as if he needed to turn onto that road.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:12:1.english: Shofars - [They] announce about him so that [people] will come to honor him.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:12:2.english: That men form a partition from abbula to sikhra - From the gate of that city until the grave.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:12:3.hebrew: נטילתה - של תורה ממנו, כנתינתה בסיני. נטילתה היינו כשמת ותלמודו בטל:
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:12:3.english: Its taking - [The taking] of the Torah from us [is] like its giving at Sinai. "Its taking" means when he dies and his study ceases.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:12:5.hebrew: ותני - משנה, אבל עדיין לא שנה לתלמידים:
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:12:5.english: And studied - Mishnah, but he has not yet taught [it] to students.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:1:1.english: As she is - According to her beauty and her distinction, they praise her.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:1:2.english: Graceful - A thread of grace is drawn upon her.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:1:3.hebrew: מכאן אמרו - מדברי ב"ה שאמרו ישבחנה:
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:1:3.english: From here [the Sages] said - From the words of Beit Hillel, who said one should praise her.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:1:4.english: A person's disposition should be empathetic with mankind - To act toward each and every person according to his wishes.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:2:2.english: No eye shadow - She does not need eye shadow.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:2:3.english: And no rouge - A dye that reddens the face.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:2:4.hebrew: פירכוס - קליעת שיער. זו לא כחלה ולא שרקה ולא פירכסה, והרי היא יעלת חן:
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:2:4.english: Pirkus - Braiding of hair. This [bride] has neither applied eye shadow, nor applied rouge, nor braided [her hair], and behold, she is a graceful ibex.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:3:1.english: Anyone of this [kind] - All [those] like these, ordain for us, to call them "Rabbi" and to appoint them [as] judges.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:3:2.english: Sarmisin - [Those who] distort halakhot by reversing their reasons.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:3:4.english: Ḥamisin - [Those who] say [only] a fifth of the reason.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:3:5.hebrew: טורמיסין - לא איתפרש: (טורמיסין — כי ההיא דאמר בב"ר (פ' מ"א): ״על טורמיסין למיקרב למסאנא דמטרוניתא״ — אנשים ריקנים):
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:3:5.english: Turmisin - [Its meaning] has not been explained. ([Regarding] turmisin: [it is] like that which is stated in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 41), "[Is it] for turmisin to approach the shoe of a matron?" — [meaning] empty [and worthless] people.)

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:4:1.english: From the academy - From the study hall.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:4:2.english: Master of his people - A prince among his people.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:4:4.english: Blessed is your arrival in peace - Blessed is your coming in peace.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:4:5.hebrew: בוצינא דנהורא - על שהיה קלסתר פניו מבהיק, כדאמרינן בב"ב (דף נח.): שופריה דרבי אבהו מעין שופריה דרבי יוחנן, דנפקי זיהרורית מיניה, כדמפרש התם:
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:4:5.english: Candle of illumination - Because his countenance shone, as we say in Bava Batra (58a): "The beauty of Rabbi Abbahu [is] a semblance of the beauty of Rabbi Yochanan," for rays of light would issue from him, as is explained there.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:5:1.hebrew: אתלת - שלש בדין, זורק אחת ומקבל אחת:
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:5:1.english: On three - [With] three branches; he throws one and catches one.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:5:2.english: The old man is humiliating us - For he degrades the honor of Torah scholars and conducts himself with levity.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:6:1.english: His branch - A branch of myrtle with which he would dance.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:6:2.english: His folly - That he would behave like a fool.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:6:3.english: His method [shittatei] - His way and his custom.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:7:1.english: [He] would place her on his shoulders - the bride.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:7:2.english: Like a beam - Like a mere beam, [meaning] that you do not have [improper] thoughts about her.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:8:1.hebrew: לחבבה - כשרואה הכל מסתכלים בה, נכנס יופיה בלבו:
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:8:1.english: To endear her - When [he] sees everyone looking at her, her beauty enters his heart.

Rashi on Ketubot 17a:9:1.hebrew: מעבירין - כשכלה יוצאה מבית אביה לבית חתונתה, ונושאי מת יוצאים, ובזו ובזו אוכלוסים הרבה ואין רוצין להתערב, מעבירין את המת (אפילו) דרך אחרת:
Rashi on Ketubot 17a:9:1.english: One reroutes - When a bride goes out from her father's house to her wedding house, and pallbearers are going out, and in both this [procession] and that [procession] there are large crowds and they do not want to mingle, one reroutes the corpse (even) [along] another route.

Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:10:1.hebrew: מלך שמחל על כבודו אין כבודו מחול - אע"ג דלא היה מלך גמור, כדמשמע באלו נאמרין (סוטה דף מא.), מ"מ היו נוהגין בו כבוד כמלך גמור:
Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:10:1.english: A king who relinquishes his honor, his honor is not relinquished - Even though he was not a full king, as is implied in [the chapter] Eilu Ne'emarin (Sotah 41a), nevertheless they accorded him honor like a full king.

Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:10:2.hebrew: פרשת דרכים הואי - הכא לא מצי לשנויי "מצוה שאני", כדמשני באלו נאמרין (ג"ז שם) גבי שקרא מעומד; דהתם מצוה הוא, שיש למלך לחלוק כבוד לתורה החשובה ממנו, אבל הכא ליכא מצוה, דכבודו עדיף מכבוד הכלה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:10:2.english: It was [at] a crossroads - Here, [the Gemara] could not answer, "A mitzvah is different," as it answers in [chapter] Elu Ne'emarim (this too is there) regarding [the case] where he read standing; for there it is a mitzvah, since a king must show honor to the Torah, which is greater than he, but here there is no mitzvah, since his honor takes precedence over the honor of the bride.

Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:11:1.hebrew: מבטלין תלמוד תורה להוצאת המת - וקשה, דבהלכות דרך ארץ אמר ר"ע: "תחלת תשמישי לפני חכמים, פעם אחת הייתי מהלך בדרך ומצאתי מת מצוה, ונטפלתי בו ד' מילין עד שהבאתיו לבית הקברות וקברתיו, וכשבאתי והרציתי דברי לפני ר"א ור' יהושע, אמרו לי: על כל פסיעה ופסיעה כאילו שפכת דם נקי". וי"ל, דהתם לאו משום ביטול תורה, אלא משום דמת מצוה קנה מקומו, והיה לו לקוברו במקום שמצאו. וכן משמע במס' שמחות (פ"ד), דקאמר: מת מצוה קנה מקומו, והעובר על דברי חכמים חייב מיתה, וכן אמר ר' עקיבא: "תחלת תשמישי כו'". והר"ר יהודה מקורבי"ל תירץ, דהתם משום דביטל עצמו משימוש ת"ח קאמר, דגדול שימושה יותר מלימודה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:11:1.english: One suspends the study of Torah for the removal of a corpse - And this is difficult, for in Hilkhot Derekh Eretz Rabbi Akiva said: "At the beginning of my attendance upon the Sages, I was once walking on the road and found an unattended corpse [met mitzvah], and I occupied myself with it for four mil until I brought it to the cemetery and buried it. And when I came and recounted my actions before Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, they said to me: 'For each and every step [you took], it is as if you shed innocent blood.'" And one can answer that there, [their rebuke] was not because of neglect of Torah [study], but rather because an unattended corpse acquires its place [where it lies], and he should have buried it in the place where he found it. And this is likewise implied in Tractate Semachot (chapter 4), where it states: An unattended corpse acquires its place, and one who transgresses the words of the Sages is liable to death; and so Rabbi Akiva said: "At the beginning of my attendance, etc." And Rabbi Yehudah of Corbeil answered that there, [the rebuke] was stated because he withdrew himself from attending upon Torah scholars, for serving [Torah scholars] is greater than studying [Torah].

Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:11:2.hebrew: להוצאת המת - לא במת מצוה איירי, אלא בכל המתים. ואע"ג דבפ"ק דמגילה (דף ג: ושם) אומר: "פשיטא דמת מצוה ותלמוד תורה — מת מצוה עדיף, דתניא: מבטלין ת"ת להוצאת המת", נקט מת מצוה אגב מילי אחריני דהתם, דהוו דווקא מת מצוה. והא דאמר באלו מגלחין (מו"ק דף כז:): "מת בעיר — כל בני העיר אסורים בעשיית מלאכה", ומוקי לה בדליכא חברותא, אבל אי איכא חברותא מותרין השאר — פירוש "חברותא": שנחלקו בני העיר לחבורות שתעסוק כל אחת במת שלה בפני עצמה; היינו שלא בשעת הוצאה, אבל בשעת הוצאה כולם צריכין לבא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:11:2.english: For the removal of a corpse - [The Gemara] is not speaking of a met mitzvah [an unattended corpse], rather of all corpses. And even though in the first chapter of Megillah (3b and there) it says: "It is obvious that [between] a met mitzvah and Torah study, a met mitzvah takes precedence, as it was taught [in a baraita]: One suspends Torah study for the removal of a corpse" — it mentioned met mitzvah incidentally along with the other matters there, which were specifically [about] a met mitzvah. And that which it says in [chapter] Eilu Megalchin (Moed Katan 27b): "[If there is] a corpse in the town, all the townspeople are forbidden from doing work," and [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring to a case] where there is no burial society [chavruta], whereas if there is a burial society, the rest [of the townspeople] are permitted — the explanation of "chavruta" is that the townspeople divided into groups so that each [group] attends to its own dead on its own; that is [only] when it is not the time of the funeral procession, but at the time of the funeral procession, everyone is required to come.

Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:1:1.hebrew: כלה כמות שהיא - ואם יש בה מום, ישתקו ולא ישבחוה; אי נמי, ישבחוה בדבר נאה שיש בה, כגון בעיניה או בידיה, אם הם יפות. וב"ה אומרים: ישבחוה לגמרי, דכשמזכירין מה שיש בה לשבח — מכלל דשאר לגנאי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:1:1.english: The bride as she is - And if she has a blemish, they should remain silent and not praise her; alternatively, they should praise her for something attractive that she has, such as her eyes or her hands, if they are pretty. And Beit Hillel say: They should praise her completely, for when they mention what is praiseworthy about her — it implies that the rest [of her] is shameful.

Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:1:2.hebrew: ישבחנו בעיניו או יגננו בעיניו - וב"ש סברי: אע"ג דישבחנו בעיניו, אין להם לחכמים לתקן להזקיק לומר שקר, דהתורה אמרה: "מדבר שקר תרחק":
Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:1:2.english: Should he praise it in his eyes or condemn it in his eyes - And Beit Shammai hold [that] even though he should praise it in his eyes, it is not [proper] for the Sages to institute [an obligation] compelling [people] to speak falsehood, for the Torah states: "Keep you from a false matter" (Exodus 23:7).

Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:6:1.hebrew: שיטתיה לסבא - פר"ח: לשון "שיטה והדס" (ישעיה מ"א); אע"ג דלא הוי ממש מין אחד, מ"מ שניהם מין ארז. וא"ת: ומנא ליה דבשביל כן זכה? וי"ל: דעמוד דנורא היה כעין שיבשא דהדס, כדאמרינן בבראשית רבה (פ' סא): "נחת שיבשא דנורא ואיתעבידא כעין שיבשא דהדס, ואפסקת בין דידיה לחברוהי. אמרי: חמית הדין סבא דקאי שיבשא דנורא קומיה, משום דעביד קמוהי דכלתא":
Tosafot on Ketubot 17a:6:1.english: Shittatei lesava - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: [This is] an expression of "acacia [shittah] and myrtle" (Isaiah 41:19); even though it is not literally the same species, nevertheless both are species of cedar. And if you ask: How did [Rabbi Zeira] know that it was on account of this [mitzva] that he merited [the pillar of fire]? One can answer: Because the pillar of fire was like a myrtle branch, as we say in Bereishit Rabbah (Section 61): "A branch of fire descended and became like a myrtle branch, and it separated between him and his colleagues. They said: 'Do you see this old man, before whom a branch of fire stands because of [what] he used to do before the bride?'"
